snippet.title: Hocus Pocus 2 Deletes Scenes
snippet.description:
Hocus Pocus was filled with so much magic, Disney couldn’t possibly fit it all in! Let’s explore all of these Disney deleted scenes starring Bette Midler, Sarah Jessica Parker, and Kathy Najimy as the iconic Sanderson sisters. Did you know that Hocus Pocus 2 had a completely different ending? They rushed to reshoot it months after it wrapped! There are also several hilarious moments shared between the Sanderson sisters that didn’t get to make the cut. There was an entire scene where Sarah and Mary push Winnie into a pool and as she comes out, she shocks them with a smoldering bolt of lightning! That’s one of the few scenes that didn’t get lost on the 1993 cutting room floor – there are so many we won’t ever get to watch. Have you checked out the original trailer from 1993? There are a few different deleted scenes you can catch in it. One of them is the iconic grocery store trip that the Sanderson sisters take to find ingredients to their candy crows. What are candy crows, you ask? Just another thing that was cut from the original shooting script. Originally, the Sanderson sisters would enchant children by giving them cursed candy crows, which would then possess them to make their way to the witches’ home in the woods, where they would then steal their youth. There was also an alternate ending to the original Hocus Pocus! Any Binx fans definitely want to stick around until the end to find out what almost was for their favorite talking cat.

snippet.title: Filming These House of the Dragon Scenes Was Intense
snippet.description:
House of the Dragon has some of the most intense, difficult sequences for actors to perform. Milly Alcock shared her struggle with doing certain scenes with Emily Carey as well as Matt Smith’s disdain for performing all of his intimate scenes. One of the most difficult scenes in the series has to be in episode one when Queen Aemma is trying to give birth to her and King Viserys’ song. That scene was filmed on a closed set and was so brutal for Sian Brooke. She went through at least fourteen different takes and had fourteen different dresses handmade for her. She also had a ton of uncomfortable tubing strapped underneath her in order to convey how fatal the incision was. There were also some more comedic instances, like Matt Smith getting hit in the forehead with is own sword and slicing himself a bit. The actors also struggled with the intense intimacy scenes they had to shoot. Emily Carey was only seventeen when she read the script. There were scenes with her character and King Viserys’ character that are more intimate than she was comfortable with, considering the 30-year age difference. She was concerned about shooting it, but with a brilliant intimacy coordinator and Paddy Considine’s lovely demeanor, they were able to get through it. We also get into how much of a process it was for the tournament scene – they literally built an entire colosseum from scratch. We’ll be getting into all of this and more that made House of the Dragon super intense and at times very difficult for these actors to film.

snippet.description:
Fluctuating weight like actors do in Hollywood is dangerous. We are talking about what they risked to play the parts. Dacre Montgomery wasn’t aiming for perfect with that Stranger Things bod, just authentic. Brendan Fraser returned to acting rejuvenated and ready to try something new with The Whale. And new indeed, he was carrying around close to three hundred pounds of prosthetics. So many, in fact, he was actually developing muscles to carry all the extra weight around! David Harbour dropped all that weight for Stranger Things just to pack it back on to play Santa Claus in Violent night. Mark Wahlburg only had thirty days to shoot a film and had to gain twenty pounds to do it. What he put himself through to accomplish that was just insane. Like, more insane than the documentary about the guy who only ate McDonalds for a month. Natalie Portman faced her own challenges when developing muscle due to her vegan lifestyle, getting that protein intake meant relying on substances outside of food alone. Ryan Gosling chugged back melted ice cream to gain thirty pounds only to lose it to another actor in the video! Zac Efron has openly admitted to struggling with his body image in Baywatch. Chris Hemsworth and Chris Evans both have the same stunt guy and that stunt guy had to eat nearly three dozen times a day to keep up with Hemsworth! Pattinson abandoned his morals. snippet.title: The Chaos Behind The Rings of Power
snippet.description:
Rings of Power is the next addition to the Lord of the Rings franchise we’ve all been waiting for. With stellar performances from actors like Morfydd Clark and Charlie Vickers, we couldn’t wait to dive deep into everything it has to offer. There was so much chaos behind the set, it’s a miracle they were able to deliver this series to us. One of the big things the actors struggled with was the free dive training. They had to learn to hold their breath underwater for minutes at a time – that’s no easy feat. Morfydd Clark says it doesn’t get easier, you just learn how to ignore the pain. Charlie Vickers isn’t a strong swimmer, so it didn’t help that he had so many swimming scenes. The performers really went through the wringer on that set. There were a ton of fun times on the set as well. There were a ton of pranks being pulled on the cast and crew. One in particular was pulled by Maxim Baldry – he pretended to get hurt and filmed it. Markella Kavenagh and Megan Richards were also an iconic duo – constantly singing and performing for the cast members. They built up quite a reputation with their songs. How long do you think the Orcs were in the make-up chair for? Hours and hours – they would arrive to set around midnight every day before the cast would show up around 7 AM. They were also incredibly terrifying! We’ll be getting into all of this and more – so stick around until the end!

snippet.title: 25 Alternate Endings in Disney Movies
snippet.description:
Crafting the perfect ending for a movie is no easy task. Every Disney writer knows this. Turning Red saw one charming moment cut where Mei meets one of the members from 4*Town. But also, there was a giant panda battle across Toronto. But also, at one point the panda wasn’t the problem, it was more about what kind of panda she wanted to be! A party panda? Encanto had a heartbreaking ending that led Mirabel and Abuela back to the home they had to abandon. Luca almost included sea monsters far scarier than Uncle Ugo! Soul had a ton of different potential endings. It makes sense, this movie was all about choices. Raya and the Last Dragon contemplated the movie just being Raya and no more dragons. Toy Story 4 almost saw Bo Peep break up with Woody. And before the first Toy Story got off the ground, Woody was a creepy ventriloquist doll! Frozen 2 almost saw Arendelle wiped out. Cars 3 would have paved way for Cars 4 but turns out they could fit that beat in the same script! The first draft of Coco would have seen Miguel go after someone much closer to him than his grandpa. Maui was upstaging Moana way too much. Frozen nearly saw an army of ice monsters thanks to some significant differences. The Lion King saw more flames. The Little Mermaid saw humans submerged underwater. Lilo and Stitch needed one scene completely changed after significant historical events shook the planet. Tarzan almost reversed its ending. The Jungle Book had a very dark ending with a grown-up Mowgli. If they never got past the first drafts of scripts, Disney would be an entirely different beast!

Avatar changed the face of filming forever. With the amount of technology they invented in order to make this movie, it’s no wonder it blew people’s minds when it first came out in theaters. Like the tech where they can see pandora through the camera while they're in the motion capture studio. Facial capture was taken to the next level with Avatar. They pioneered the technology that was attached to the actor’s faces so that they could capture every little detail. The animals are all hexapedal, meaning they have six legs in this world. To create these creatures, they studied real horses, but then using the new Weta tech, they were able to create creatures from the inside out with musculature attached to bone structure. They set the standard in the industry. Before Sam Worthington and Zoe Saldaña ever came on board to play Jake Sully and Neytiri, they cast two temporary actors to play the roles and create a clip to prove they were ready. We’re looking shot-by-shot at what was up behind the scenes of the most tech-heavy movie ever created and also taking a peek at Avatar: The Way of Water and how it's changing the filming scene again, how long Kate Winslet can hold her breath for and how much water tech was invented.
